domain.headline: Reuters reports Kpler total September oil exports at 18.6 million bpd; its separate seven-country crude and condensate series rose to 14.7 million bpd from 10.8 in August. Kpler counted 21 LNG cargoes exiting Hormuz in September, followed by four Qatar-loaded vessels reappearing outside on Oct 2-3. Dark AIS may omit passages; no verified reopening agreement was found.

sources.title: Oil prices slide about 2% as US, Iran explore path out of war | Reuters
sources.note: Reuters reported Brent settled at 104.32 USD/bbl on Sep 25, down 2.1%, as truce hopes outweighed attack risk. The article also reported Brent at 105.11 at 05:41 GMT, six Houthi missiles intercepted near Taif/Yanbu, and no resumption of Yanbu tanker loadings.

sources.title: Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship oil transfers reach limit as Saudi exports surge | Reuters
sources.note: Reuters reported September Saudi crude exports via Hormuz on track for 3.6 million bpd, while Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship operations reached capacity. A $1.27 million/day Middle East-to-China VLCC time-charter quote was reported for Sep 21.

sources.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions linger as Iran and US move further from a deal
sources.note: Al Jazeera reported Sep 27 that Tehran instructed shipping companies to use a temporary Iran-approved Hormuz route and pay fees; full reopening remains conditional on ending the US blockade. Reports of explosions were attributed to Iranian media and were not confirmed by Iranian authorities.

sources.title: Oil prices settle down 2.5% on signs Middle East exports recovering
sources.note: Reuters reported Saudi Arabia resumed Yanbu tanker loadings after restarting East-West Pipeline operations. Reuters reported Sep 29 Brent settlement at $102.59/bbl and WTI at $89.38/bbl; these are separate settlement observations from Yahoo snapshots.

sources.title: Three oil tankers hit by projectiles in Hormuz strait on Tuesday, Marisks says
sources.note: Marisks reported three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting Hormuz on Sep 29. Reuters names Al Ruwais, Mersin Prosperity and Sinbad; Marisks said AIS transponders were off.

sources.title: Iran says it receives US response to latest proposal
sources.note: Iran said it received a US response to its latest proposal. An official briefed on the talks said the parties disagree about the sequence of steps; no reopening agreement was reported.

sources.title: Qatar-linked LNG traffic through Hormuz strait picks up despite conflict
sources.note: Reuters/LSEG/Kpler tracked GasLog Skagen off Sri Lanka Sep 27 with a Ras Laffan cargo. Al Shamal reappeared outside Hormuz around Sep 24-25; Al Ghashamiya delivered to Dahej Sep 24. The report describes individual sightings and dark AIS transits, not a complete comparable weekly LNG count.

sources.title: Oil jumps 4% on reports China halts fuel exports, US troops head to Middle East
sources.note: Reuters reports Chinese refiners suspended oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, citing four sources. The new front-month December Brent contract settled at $102.31, +4.37%; WTI settled at $92.87, +2.71%, on Oct 1. Reuters cites a Wall Street Journal report that the US is sending a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 additional troops; these deployments are reported plans.
